note: One of the largest campgrounds on the San Juan NF, on Vallecito Creek beside the Weminuche Wilderness, ~8,000 ft, ~3 mi up County Road 500 from the Vallecito community (Vallecito Reservoir 4 mi). Sites near the creek fill first. Vallecito Creek Trail (hiking/horse) starts at the entrance, with hitching posts and a livestock dock but no horse camping; fly and lure fishing only; seven fee picnic sites along the creek. Concessionaire-run. --Claude

flags: Electric count conflict: FS page says '33 reservable sites, 3 with electricity, and 47 non-reservable sites'; recreation.gov catalog has 79 sites with 13 STANDARD ELECTRIC 50-amp sites, all reservable (LOOP W 005-008, 011, 013-016; LOOP B 027-030), and 45 reservable sites in all. Either way the electric sites are public and bookable, so electric 50 stands (catalog; rates show a $45 electric rate). Booking note gives both counts.

The (661) 702-1420 / rlynd@goexplorus.com contact is the concessionaire (Explorus); the old note's 'Rocky Mountain Recreation' is not on either page, so dropped from the note.

Flood: the SJNF flood alert (updated 10/27/26) reports widespread damage from the Oct 22-25, 2026 storm and says assessment will take days to weeks; it lists no Vallecito Campground or County Road 500 entry. The October 2025 flood destroyed the Vallecito Creek Trail's wilderness bridges (replacement not before 2027). The FS campground page (current conditions) says the campground 'remains partially open ... through November 15th, 2026'. CR 500 is a La Plata County road; I found no county closure for it. Worth a recheck in spring 2027.
Rig length: FS 'Max RV size = 45 ft'; catalog vehicle maximums 28-50 (one 20). No criteria problem.
Pin 37.47571,-107.54706 is near the entrance road ~215 m SW of the FS point (37.4776,-107.5466); 28 m from the nearest site, 167 m from the site centroid. OK.

Waterfront 'creekside' kept: on NAIP Vallecito Creek (~15-20 m wide whitewater) runs along the east side of the campground. LOOP B sites 001-009 sit ~10-40 m from the water (003 and 004 closest, under thin pine canopy); FS 'Those near the creek fill up quickly'. The other loops (C, D, W) are 100 m+ back. The creek is a large mountain stream; creekside matches the agency's own word for it.
